ns2:section.sectionText: Topic: Women and the Family, Law, and Colonial Modernity in South Asia, the Middle East, and North Africa Description: The history of “the family” is an important topic in colonial and post-colonial South Asia, the Middle East, and North Africa (SAMENA). Contemporary debates on human rights, family law, gender, and sexuality are better understood in light of the re-imagining of “family” in modern times and efforts, through legislation, to promote a modern family ideal. A comparative approach will enable us to identify transnational patterns of change in SAMENA. Modern social constructions of the family have been entangled with constructions (or reconstructions) of the nation and gender. Legal systems were reformed in conformity with European norms, resulting in the creation of “family law,” which has become an arena in which conflicts over the roles of women and the family are fought. We will range from the pre-modern era to recent developments in selected SAMENA countries. Area content will be at least 25% African, 25% Middle Eastern, and 25% South Asian.
